A permission alone is not proof of malware — what matters is whether it fits the app’s purpose.
Reads the screen and taps for you. Legitimate: screen readers and assistive tools. Suspicious: when a game, flashlight or “update” app asks.
Hinders uninstall and can lock the screen. Legitimate: corporate MDM or find-my-phone. Suspicious: in ordinary apps.
Reads all notifications, including codes. Legitimate: smartwatch or fitness-band apps. Suspicious: unknown apps with internet access.
Asks to install or remove apps. Legitimate: app stores, file managers. Suspicious: ordinary apps that download other APKs.
Draws over other apps. Legitimate: chat bubbles, screen filters. Suspicious: fake login screens over banking apps.
Reads or sends SMS. Legitimate: the default SMS app. Suspicious: other apps — stealing bank codes or paid SMS.
Sees your call log. Legitimate: dialer or caller-ID apps. Suspicious: in other apps.
Makes calls or reads phone details. Legitimate: messengers, dialers. Suspicious: calls to premium numbers.
Reads contacts. Legitimate: messengers. Suspicious: apps that have no need for them.
Accesses location. Legitimate: maps, taxi, weather. Suspicious: constant background tracking.
Records audio. Legitimate: calls and voice messages. Suspicious: hidden background recording.
Uses the camera. Legitimate: photos, video calls, QR. Suspicious: apps without such a feature.
Accesses files. Legitimate: gallery, file manager. Suspicious: ordinary apps demanding full file access.
Sees all installed apps. Legitimate: antivirus, launchers. Suspicious: unknown apps looking for banking apps.
Routes traffic through itself. Legitimate: VPN services. Suspicious: non-VPN apps.
Changes system settings. Legitimate: brightness or sound tools. Suspicious: in other apps.
Sees device accounts. Legitimate: email, sync. Suspicious: in unknown apps.
Runs in the background or at boot. Legitimate: alarms, messengers. Suspicious: combined with other risky permissions.
Access to personal data. Check that it fits the app’s purpose.
